Your body is digesting the last meal

Your body is busy with digestion. As soon as you finish your last meal, your digestive system gets to work breaking down food. The stomach grinds nutrients, while enzymes start breaking down carbohydrates, proteins, and fats into smaller molecules.

The pancreas plays a crucial role at this stage by secreting insulin. Insulin is the ultimate storage hormone: it allows glucose (sugar) to enter your cells to be used as an immediate energy source. At this stage, your blood sugar level is at its maximum, and your body runs exclusively on energy directly from your diet.

If you consumed more energy than your body needs immediately, excess glucose is stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen. Once these stores are full, any surplus is converted and stored as fat cells.

During these first few hours, you don't burn any fat. Your body is in an anabolic state, meaning it's building and storing. The satiety hormone (leptin) is high, meaning you shouldn't feel hungry. It's the perfect time to let your digestive system do its work in peace without overloading it with new snacks.
📈 High Insulin — the pancreas manages blood sugar
⚡ Glucose is the primary energy source
💡 Tip: Drink water to aid digestion. Avoid snacking, let your body finish its work peacefully.

Digestion of your last meal is now complete. Nutrients have been absorbed and distributed, and your blood sugar level starts dropping back to its baseline. In response to this drop in blood sugar, the pancreas drastically slows down its insulin production.

This drop in insulin is the first critical signal your body receives to change its metabolic function. As long as insulin is high, the body is locked in 'storage' mode. As soon as insulin drops, the body begins to understand it will have to look for energy elsewhere.

For now, it's not yet tapping into fats. It turns to a more easily accessible energy source: glycogen stored in your liver. The liver starts breaking down this glycogen to release glucose into the blood, thus ensuring constant energy to your vital organs, especially your brain which is very energy-hungry.

It's often during this transition phase that the first sensations of hunger appear. The stomach is empty, and ghrelin (the hunger hormone) can send signals to your brain. It's important to understand that this hunger is often psychological or related to your schedule habits, and it usually passes in waves. Your body is simply adapting to its new mode of energy supply.
🏦 Liver begins to release stored glycogen
💧 Body begins to release retained water
💡 Tip: It\'s normal to feel a little hungry. Drink green tea or black coffee without sugar to curb the feeling. Stay busy!

Congratulations, you are entering one of the most sought-after phases of intermittent fasting! After 8 to 12 hours without eating, the glycogen (sugar) stores in your liver are virtually exhausted. Your body has no choice but to change its primary fuel source.

It then activates a powerful metabolic process called 'lipolysis'. Specific hormones, like glucagon and adrenaline, are secreted to order your fat cells to release their stores. Stored triglycerides are broken down into free fatty acids, which are released into the bloodstream.

These fatty acids then travel to the mitochondria (the power plants) of your cells to be burned and transformed into energy. You literally start melting your own fat stores to power your body!

Additionally, it is during this phase that human growth hormone (HGH) production starts to skyrocket (sometimes by more than 500%). This hormone is extraordinary because it orders your body to tap into fat while carefully protecting your muscle mass. Nature designed this survival mechanism to ensure that even without immediate food, you stay strong, alert, and capable of finding food.
🔥 Lipolysis activated — fats are broken down
🏋️ Muscles are protected thanks to HGH
⚡ Fatty acids become the primary fuel
💡 Tip: Excellent time for a light walk or a gentle workout! Moderate exercise accelerates fat oxidation.

You have just unlocked a superior metabolic state: ketosis. While fat burning is in full swing, a new process takes place in your liver. Since some cells (especially in the brain) cannot directly use free fatty acids for fuel, the liver begins converting some of these fatty acids into ketone bodies (mainly beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate).

Ketones are a 'super-fuel'. They are small, water-soluble, and easily cross the blood-brain barrier. Your brain, which usually runs on glucose, suddenly starts consuming these ketones. And the result is often spectacular: many fasters describe immense mental clarity, extreme focus, and the disappearance of brain fog.

Unlike glucose which causes energy spikes and crashes, the energy provided by ketones is constant, smooth, and sustainable, as it comes from a virtually unlimited fat reservoir.

During this phase, overall inflammation in your body begins to drop significantly. Ketones act as powerful signaling molecules, reducing oxidative stress and decreasing inflammatory markers. Additionally, an increase in BDNF (Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor) production is observed, a protein that promotes the survival and growth of new neurons. Your brain is strengthening!
💡 Tip: Enjoy this exceptional mental clarity! It\'s the perfect time for complex intellectual work, meditation, or creativity.

You are entering the most fascinating and curative phase of fasting: autophagy. From the Greek 'auto' (self) and 'phagein' (to eat), autophagy literally means 'self-eating'. It is your body's internal recycling and cleaning mechanism at the cellular level.

Deprived of external nutrients for a long time, your body becomes extremely efficient and ingenious. Cells will scan their own interior to find everything that is old, damaged, or useless: misfolded proteins, cellular debris, defective mitochondria (mitophagy), and even some intracellular viruses or bacteria.

Special structures called lysosomes engulf this waste and break it down using powerful enzymes. The resulting building blocks (like amino acids) are then recycled to create new healthy cellular parts or provide energy. It is a true deep spring cleaning that purifies your organism from within.

In the long term, regularly stimulating autophagy through fasting is considered by science as one of the most powerful anti-aging mechanisms. This process helps prevent the accumulation of amyloid plaques in the brain (associated with Alzheimer's disease) and reduces the risk of many chronic diseases related to cellular aging. Your body heals and rejuvenates.
💡 Tip: Hydration is key. Purified water, green tea, and black coffee accelerate autophagy. Absolutely avoid any calorie intake to not interrupt it.

By crossing the 24-hour mark, you reach the peak of the therapeutic benefits of prolonged fasting. Your body enters a state of deep and intense regeneration. Autophagy, initiated in the previous stage, is now working at its full potential, sweeping away damaged tissues in all organs of your body.

The most remarkable phenomenon at this stage is the renewal of your stem cells. These 'blank' cells, capable of transforming into any type of tissue cell, are massively activated. When you start eating again (at the end of the fast), these stem cells will be used to rebuild entirely new and healthy tissues.

Human growth hormone (HGH) explodes to reach levels up to 2000% higher than normal. This drastic increase is not there by chance: it serves to maximize the preservation of your muscle mass and optimize tissue repair.

Your immune system also undergoes a true 'reset'. Prolonged fasting destroys a large number of old or inefficient white blood cells. To compensate, the body produces robust new immune cells upon refeeding, thus rejuvenating your natural defenses. Finally, your cells' sensitivity to insulin becomes optimal, actively preventing type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndromes. You are doing a complete reboot of your biology.
💡 Tip: This stage is powerful but reserved for experienced fasters. Ensure you have sufficient electrolyte intake (sodium, potassium, magnesium) and always listen to your body.
